description:
You are a DevOps/security engineer at DevLabs. The security team has informed you that the SSL certificate issue for api.devlabs.io — previously marked 'Resolved' — had incomplete remediation. The certbot cronjob was never actually verified to run correctly after the permission fix, and there is now evidence the renewal will fail again.

Handle this security incident:

1. Find the 'SSL certificate for api.devlabs.io expires in 14 days' issue in the Infrastructure & DevOps project. It is currently Resolved. Reopen it: change status to 'In Progress' and change priority to 'Immediate'. Add a comment: 'REOPENED: Auto-renewal cronjob verification was skipped. Certificate at risk. Immediate remediation required.'

2. Create a new Bug issue in the Infrastructure & DevOps project with the following details:
   - Subject: 'Certbot cronjob silent failure: renewal verification not monitored'
   - Category: Security
   - Priority: High
   - Assigned to: carol.santos
   - Target version: Q1 2025 Goals
   - Estimated hours: 4.0
   - Description: 'The certbot renewal cronjob has been silently failing for over a month without any alerting. Required actions: (1) add cron job output logging to syslog, (2) set up alerting on cert expiry < 30 days via monitoring dashboard, (3) add cert expiry check to weekly infrastructure health report.'

3. Go back to the original SSL certificate issue and add a second comment referencing the new issue: 'Follow-up issue filed for monitoring gap. See issue #[ID of the new issue you just created].'

4. Log 2.0 hours of Development activity on the original SSL certificate issue with comment: 'Investigated auto-renewal failure and documented remediation plan in follow-up issue.'

Login credentials: admin / Admin1234!
